objective: Replicate Anic, Barbon, Seiz and Zarattini (2025, arXiv:2510.26228) 'ChatGPT in Systematic Investing' on Open Composer's own PIT largest-500 universe: does DeepSeek-scored, news-conditioned re-ranking/re-weighting of a top-2-decile 12-1 momentum pool (the paper's own basic prompt, m=50, eta=5, 15% cap) raise Sharpe over a plain rule baseline B, after 10/20bp costs, in a CLEAN evaluation window that starts strictly after the scoring model's own disclosed knowledge cutoff -- versus a headline-shuffle placebo P and a random-selection control R?
target_regime_and_horizon: US large/liquid equities (PIT largest-500 by dollar ADV), monthly rebalance, long-only, m=50 concentrated book. Validity is limited to this specific mechanism (LLM re-ranks/re-weights an already-passing rule-based momentum book using recent firm-specific news) and to the CLEAN window: formations 2026-05-29, 2026-06-30, 2026-07-31, 2026-08-31 (first month-end after DeepSeek V4 Flash's disclosed April-2026 knowledge cutoff through the last panel date, 2026-09-17). No claim is made this generalizes to other universes, other LLMs, other news sources, or a longer sample; the CLEAN window is thin (4 formations) by construction, mirroring the target paper's own thin (15-month) OOS window.
existing_solution_comparison: The mechanism (LLM reads pre-supplied, timestamped firm-specific news to filter/re-weight an already-passing rule-based momentum book) is not new to this repo: dir:llm_acceptance_judge_forward_shadow / H-20260916-04 already designs a weekly DeepSeek keep/half/skip judge on the T1 momentum top-50 using news + insider filings + 8-K dates, forward-shadow evaluated (status: proposed, budget 2 variants, used 0), per I-20260928-03's ranked recommendation #1 (2026-09-28). This round is the SAME mechanism family but a DISTINCT, narrower, backtest-first test: it replicates the target paper's own specific published design (continuous 0-1 score -> rank -> re-weight by Wi=E*eta^score, not a 3-way keep/half/skip judge; top-2-decile pool not top-50; monthly not weekly; no insider/8-K features, news only) with a placebo and random control this repo can run cheaply on 2024-2026 data before committing to H-20260916-04's slower forward-only protocol. A positive result here would be independent, backtest-based evidence the news-conditioned-momentum-filter mechanism can work locally; it does not replace H-20260916-04's forward-shadow test (different scoring scheme, different pool size, different data layers) but would raise the prior for running it. dir:news_attention_features (H-20260916-02, refuted: simple count/novelty news features have no signal) is a different, much simpler mechanism (mechanical counting, not LLM-read content) and is distinguished, not re-run, here. The T1 momentum book (open_composer.research.signal_card, as used by scripts/run_h20260924_02_momentum_crash_guard.py) supplies B's construction unchanged (12-1 momentum, top decile, monthly).
remaining_evidence_gap: Whether DeepSeek (not the paper's ChatGPT-4o-mini), scoring anonymized headlines from Open Composer's own Alpaca/Benzinga news_packets store (not the paper's Stock News API), on the PIT largest-500 universe (not literal S&P 500 membership), produces a re-ranking that beats the plain momentum rule after 10/20bp costs in a genuinely post-cutoff window -- and, critically, whether any apparent lift survives a headline-shuffle placebo (rules out 'broadening the pool to 100 names plus re-weighting noise helps regardless of news content') and beats random selection from the same pool (rules out 'any re-weighting away from flat top-50 helps'). None of this has been tested locally; only the paper's own (different model, different data, different universe) result exists.
negative_experiments_checked: dir:news_attention_features / H-20260916-02 (refuted): mechanical news count/novelty features carry no signal on this repo's data -- distinguished above; this round tests LLM-read content, not counts. reports/research/iterations/h20260923_14_news_hf_reaction (H-20260923-14, refuted): SUE re-dated to 8-K acceptance time loses to a redated placebo (t=1.06<3); a different signal (earnings surprise timing) and a different placebo design (calendar redate, not headline shuffle), not the same claim as this round's news-conditioned momentum re-ranking. No prior local test of LLM-scored news re-ranking a momentum book has been run to completion; H-20260916-04 is proposed but not yet executed (budget 2, used 0).
cost_and_execution_assumptions: Signal decided at the month-end session close; fill at the next session's open; 10bp and 20bp per side on sum|delta weight| (open_composer.research.signal_card. book_returns), matching this repo's frozen G1-G5 cost contract. DeepSeek scoring cost is borne by the owner-configured endpoint (not Claude Code subscription tokens), reusing scripts/score_earnings_text.py's client, credential loading, rate-limit backoff and disk cache, per scripts/score_h20260928_16_sentiment_accel.py and scripts/score_h20260928_17_filing_risk_labels.py's established pattern. Concurrency kept low (sequential calls, checkpointed, resumable) because another agent is using the same endpoint concurrently; a 429 or any 'limit'/'quota' response pauses the batch and writes next_try_at.json rather than retrying aggressively.
stop_condition: Continue (to a forward-shadow follow-on, e.g. informing H-20260916-04's design) only if, in the CLEAN window at 10bp: Sharpe(L) >= Sharpe(B) + 0.10, AND P's Sharpe improvement over B is < 50% of L's improvement over B, AND L's Sharpe beats R's median Sharpe (5 seeds). If any one of these three fails, the verdict is refuted: no LLM news-conditioned re-ranking is added to any live or forward-tracked book on this evidence, and the queue is not touched. Reopen only with a new disclosed data source, a new LLM, or new local news coverage -- not by re-tuning the paper's own hyperparameters (m, eta, cap) or by cherry-picking the CLEAN window boundary after seeing results.

sources.claim: Anic, Barbon, Seiz and Zarattini (2025, arXiv:2510.26228) report that in the out-of-sample period (Jan 2024-Mar 2025, after ChatGPT 4.0 mini's Oct 2023 pre-training cutoff), the LLM-enhanced momentum strategy's Sharpe ratio is 1.06 versus 0.79 for the baseline momentum strategy, net of 2bps costs.
sources.market_and_period: US S&P 500 constituents (paper) / US PIT largest-500 (this round), 2019-2026
sources.applicability: Sets the informational comparison target for L's OOS Sharpe and grounds the look-ahead-control design (clean window must start after the scoring model's own cutoff, mirroring the paper's Oct-2023-cutoff logic).
sources.limitations: OOS window is only 15 months and contains no crisis/drawdown period; the paper's own LLM-vs-baseline alpha regression is significant only at the 10% level.
sources.independent_replication: Not yet independently replicated (posted 2025-10-30); this round is itself an independent replication attempt on a different (US PIT largest-500, DeepSeek-scored) data and model setup.

sources.claim: The paper's re-weighting rule for the LLM-enhanced portfolio is Wi = E * eta^LLM_Score_i, where E is the baseline (equal- or value-weight) share, LLM_Score_i is the score normalized to [-1, 1], and eta is a scaling parameter optimized to 5 on the validation set; weights are then renormalized to sum to one, with an optional 15% per-stock cap.
sources.market_and_period: US S&P 500 constituents (paper) / US PIT largest-500 (this round), 2019-2026
sources.applicability: L's per-stock weight is computed as Wi = E * eta^score_i (eta=5), 15% cap, renormalized to sum 1; E is fixed to equal weight (1/m) rather than the paper's own optimal value-weighted E, disclosed as a deviation because this repo has no reliable point-in-time market-cap feature and because using the same equal-weight E as baseline B isolates the LLM re-ranking/tilt effect.
sources.limitations: The PDF text extraction renders the exponent as plain text ("eta LLM_Scorei") with the superscript lost; read as an exponential tilt (Wi = E * eta^score_i) because (a) eta is described as a 'scaling parameter' and 'weight multiplier', (b) scores range over [-1, 1] so a linear eta*score would make some baseline-positive weights negative for a long-only book, which the paper never discusses, and (c) an exponential form keeps every weight positive across the full score range (eta^-1=0.2x to eta^1=5x at eta=5), matching the paper's own description of eta=5 as indicating a 'meaningful' and 'confidently exploited' dynamic range. No appendix with a clearer typeset formula was found in the 26-page PDF.
sources.independent_replication: Not independently replicated; this is this round's own reading of the primary source.

sources.claim: The paper's validation-set-optimal hyperparameter configuration selects monthly rebalancing, a 1-day news lookback, a 21-day lookahead, the 'basic' prompt, m=50 selected stocks, a 15% per-stock weight cap, value-weighted initial allocation, and eta=5.
sources.market_and_period: US S&P 500 constituents (paper) / US PIT largest-500 (this round), 2019-2026
sources.applicability: L uses m=50 unchanged from the paper. This round's own lookback (30 days, cap 20 headlines) and rebalance (monthly) deviate from the paper's optimal 1-day lookback -- disclosed deviation, since a 1-day news lookback would leave most candidate-months with zero qualifying headlines given this repo's lower news density outside mega-caps.
sources.limitations: Optimal on the paper's own S&P 500 / ChatGPT-4o-mini validation set (Oct 2019-Dec 2023); not re-optimized for our universe, DeepSeek model, or cost assumptions -- used as preregistered, not tuned, per this round's anti-overfitting rule.

sources.claim: When a stock-day has no relevant news, the paper treats the missing LLM score as zero (on the normalized [-1, 1] scale), representing a neutral stance.
sources.market_and_period: US S&P 500 constituents (paper) / US PIT largest-500 (this round), 2019-2026
sources.applicability: A candidate with zero qualifying anonymized headlines in the 30-day lookback gets a normalized score of 0 (raw 0.5) without a DeepSeek call, per the brief's own preregistered fallback and the paper's rule.
sources.limitations: Described for the daily-score panel used in the paper's summary statistics, not stated separately for the monthly-rebalance production rule, but is the only no-news rule the paper states.

sources.claim: Glasserman & Lin (2023, arXiv:2309.17322) find that removing a company's identifiers from news text before LLM sentiment scoring (anonymization) improves in-sample trading performance versus using the original headlines, indicating the 'distraction effect' (general knowledge about the named company interfering with sentiment measurement) has a larger impact than look-ahead bias for their sample.
sources.market_and_period: US S&P 500 constituents (paper) / US PIT largest-500 (this round), 2019-2026
sources.applicability: scripts/score_h20260928_22_news_momentum.py anonymizes every headline (company name and ticker replaced with 'the company') for both L and P, following this paper's method, before sending text to DeepSeek.
sources.limitations: Findings are for GPT sentiment scoring of news headlines on a different (older GPT, different universe) setup; motivates our anonymization design, not a direct performance transfer.
sources.independent_replication: Also referenced by arXiv:2601.13770 (Look-Ahead-Bench) and arXiv:2512.23847 as a standard anonymization-bias baseline, per this round's web search.

sources.claim: He, Lv, Manela and Wu (2025, arXiv:2502.21206) show that LLM training data can introduce lookahead bias and training leakage in social-science and financial applications, and that lookahead bias is model- and application-specific -- motivating chronologically consistent (only-past-data) training and, by extension, evaluation windows that start strictly after a model's own disclosed knowledge cutoff.
sources.market_and_period: US S&P 500 constituents (paper) / US PIT largest-500 (this round), 2019-2026
sources.applicability: Grounds the CLEAN-vs-contaminated window split and the requirement to report contaminated months separately, never counting them toward the verdict.
sources.limitations: Proposes training chronologically consistent models (ChronoBERT/ChronoGPT) rather than post-hoc cutoff-based evaluation of an off-the-shelf model; we use the weaker (but only locally feasible) control of restricting the verdict window to after the model's disclosed cutoff, disclosed as a limitation relative to their approach.
sources.independent_replication: Cited directly by Anic et al. (2025, our target paper, reference list) as grounding for the same OOS-cutoff logic.

cheapest_decisive_test.action: Compute B (rule-only, no DeepSeek calls) and R (random selection, no DeepSeek calls) first for the full panel -- both are free. Then score L for the 4 CLEAN-window formations only (~100 candidates x 4 months = ~400 DeepSeek calls, before no-news skips) and check the stop/continue rule before spending any further budget on the full 2024-2026 informational period or on P.
cheapest_decisive_test.pass_condition: L's CLEAN-window Sharpe at 10bp clears Sharpe(B)+0.10 -- if it doesn't, the full informational-period L scoring and the P placebo scoring are moot for the verdict (P and R are only needed to confirm a real CLEAN-window lift, not to produce one).
cheapest_decisive_test.falsification_condition: L's CLEAN-window Sharpe at 10bp does not clear Sharpe(B)+0.10.
